title: Bix's classical background
summary: Hug hears Debussy in Bix and links his classical knowledge with New Orleans music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Well, do you hear, for instance, do you hear Debussy in that? Do you hear other...
I can hear it. Oh, definitely. And there it should. I think Bix was basically, well, he had a good education in classical music. Although he may not have actually had the concert training, you know.
He knew the class, he had a good classical background, and I think that with that, combined with his feeling for jazz, and his mixing of the New Orleans music with his knowledge of classics.
Well, In the Mist is a good example of that.
In the Mist is a good example.
It's played in the old style, but yeah, it's got all that.

It's embellished with a lot of progressive harmonies, yes. That's a good way to put it. That's always the way I felt about it. It's old fashioned, yet it's new. And no matter how many times you play it, it sounds that way. It always comes out the same.
